editorial.headline: A Nationally Open Footwear Trade, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This specialised retail activity spans footwear in many materials and markets, open nationally to foreign investment but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Footwear retail is the subject here: specialised sales of shoes, sandals and other footwear made from leather, artificial leather, plastic, rubber, fabric or wood. The scope is broad enough to include adult men’s and women’s shoes, children’s shoes, sports shoes, sandal shoes, sandals, slippers and health shoes. What joins them is the retail focus and the footwear category itself, rather than one particular material, customer age or use case.

The activity is open at every stated business scale: micro, small, medium and large. That matters because the classification gives a single retail frame for a business whose assortment may range across formal shoes, casual sandals, children’s footwear and specialist health footwear. The record therefore describes a defined commercial activity with room for operations at each of those scales, while keeping its centre of gravity in specialised retail.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is open. A PMA business may have foreign ownership of up to 100%, so there is no national foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. The Bali position, however, is decisive for anyone planning to register a PMA business on the island: a foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. Bali marks it as blocked by risk class. At the large-business scale, its OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope, bringing it within Bali’s moratorium. The result is not a softer local qualification on an otherwise available registration; it is a block on PMA registration in Bali.

That distinction is the practical one to hold onto. The national setting remains open, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, but Bali applies an island-wide, permanent restriction to all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA. The record identifies the Bali moratorium as taking effect in May 2026. For this footwear-retail activity, national openness and Bali availability therefore point in different directions: the former permits full foreign ownership, while the latter prevents PMA registration on the island.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness and Bali availability point in different directions: full foreign ownership is permitted nationally, while PMA registration is blocked on the island.
